$comment: Anchor home domains the scheduled attester probes.
Adding a domain here does NOT assert anything about it — the job probes it
and records whatever it finds, including a total failure. That is the point:
a registry is only useful if it is willing to record that an anchor does not
work. Open a PR to add one.
Adding an anchor (manual procedure): the Stellar Anchor Directory (anchors.stellar.org)
is a human-facing web app. As of 2026-10-18 it publishes no JSON feed or API (/api/anchors
redirects to an HTML page), so this fleet is curated by hand, not seeded automatically.
To add an anchor: (1) find it in the directory or on the anchor's own site and confirm its
home domain publishes a stellar.toml; (2) run `pnpm probe:anchor <domain>` to confirm it
responds; (3) add a structured entry to `anchors` and the domain to `domains`, then open a
PR. Never invent domains: every added entry must come from the directory or the anchor's
own site. See docs/operations.md section 0.
testanchor.stellar.org is the SDF test anchor. It advertises SEP-31 but returns
an empty receive list, so it attests as NOT serving SEP-31: a useful demonstration
that the registry reports capability rather than claims. It is also the SDF's
reference SEP-6/SEP-24 anchor on testnet; see corridors/testanchor-sep6.corridor.yaml
(endpoints read from its stellar.toml, 2026-10-17).
cowrie.exchange is a real production anchor (Cowrie Exchange, Lagos, Nigeria;
see corridors/ng-cowrie.corridor.yaml). Confirmed 2026-08-11 by running the
probe against it directly: SEP-10 auth and SEP-31 (receives NGNT, USDC) both
pass; no SEP-38 quote server is published.
mint.zeam.money is Zeam (South Africa; see corridors/zeam.corridor.yaml).
Confirmed 2026-10-17 by running the probe against it directly: SEP-10 signed
a challenge and got a JWT, SEP-38 returned a firm quote, SEP-12 answered, and
SEP-31 /info receives USDC. It advertises no TRANSFER_SERVER, so SEP-6 is not
on offer even though the Anchor Directory entry lists it as a supported
standard — the toml, not the directory, decides which protocol we can drive.
stellar.org and lobstr.co were probed by hand during development and already
hold records in the registry. They are listed here because a record nobody
refreshes decays into a stale row the scheduled job will never touch — the
registry's whole claim is that staleness is visible AND fixable, so every
domain it holds belongs in this list.
BlindPay appears in the Stellar Anchor Directory for Argentina, Brazil,
Colombia, Mexico, and the United States, but the entry publishes no website
or toml_file. BlindPay's official home domain is blindpay.com; its
https://blindpay.com/.well-known/stellar.toml returned HTTP 403 on
2026-10-16, so no SEP-31 receive capability was verified and no corridor
manifest was added. This records an inconclusive probe, not a claim of
SEP-6 or SEP-24 support.
mykobo.co is a real EUR anchor (MyKobo, Warsaw, Poland), listed in the Stellar
Anchor Directory. Its stellar.toml advertises SEP-6, SEP-24 and SEP-31, but the
host it publishes for those APIs (stellar.mykobo.co) does not resolve, so the
SEP-10 and SEP-31 probes fail and no corridor manifest is written. Probed
2026-10-16; MyKobo's status page listed the Anchor service as down at the time.
connect.clickpesa.com is ClickPesa (Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda; sourced from
https://anchors.stellar.org/?s=ClickPesa). Probed 2026-10-17: toml_fetch fails
(DNS ENODATA / getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; clickpesa.com returns HTTP 404). SEP-31
is not functional and no manifest is written; blocked on active stellar.toml/SEP-6.
coins.ph is Coins.ph (Philippines), added from the Stellar Anchor Directory.
Probe result reported by the contributor on 2026-10-16: SEP-24/SEP-6 only, no SEP-31
receive side answers, so no corridor manifest is written. Blocked on SEP-6 support.
vibrantapp.com is Vibrant (Argentina; SDF/Sunship non-custodial wallet). Not
listed in anchors.stellar.org. Probed 2026-10-17: toml_fetch returns HTTP 451
(vibrant.cash returns marketing HTML without anchor SEPs). Vibrant is a wallet,
not an anchor, and serves no SEP-31 receive endpoint; no manifest is written.
anclap.com.ar is Anclap (Argentina / LatAm, ARS and other LatAm payouts), added
from the Stellar Anchor Directory for issue #231. Probe output and directory link
are recorded in the PR; no SEP-31 receive side has been verified, so no corridor
manifest is written. Blocked on SEP-6/SEP-24 unless the probe shows otherwise.
testanchor.stellar.org is the SDF test anchor. It currently advertises SEP-31
and returns an empty receive list, so it attests as NOT serving SEP-31 — a
useful demonstration that the registry reports capability rather than claims.
stellar.moneygram.com, mercuryo.io, lightnet.io, owlting.com, arf.one and
stellar-sep-24.banxa.com were added for the ng-cn RMB off-ramp research (#230):
they are the Stellar Anchor Directory entries listing China, Hong Kong or
Singapore that publish a stellar.toml or claim a SEP. None advertises SEP-31
or a CNY/CNH/HKD asset; see corridors/ng-cn.corridor.yaml for the probe results
of 2026-10-18. Their countries are the directory's listing, not attested facts.
MoneyGram Access (stellar.moneygram.com; https://anchors.stellar.org/?search=MoneyGram)
was probed 2026-10-22: TOML advertises SEP-1/10/24 and USDC; TOML fetch passes,
SEP-10 challenge returns HTTP 400, and no SEP-31 receive endpoint is published.
No corridor manifest is written; blocked on SEP-6/24 adapter support.
flutterwave.com is Flutterwave (Nigeria/Africa payments provider). Not listed
in anchors.stellar.org (https://anchors.stellar.org/?search=Flutterwave).
Probed 2026-10-19: toml_fetch returns HTTP 404 (https://flutterwave.com/.well-known/stellar.toml).
Flutterwave publishes no Stellar anchor or SEP-31 receive endpoint; no manifest is written.
bitso.com is Bitso (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico; sourced from
https://anchors.stellar.org/?search=Bitso, where the entry claims SEP-31 and
website https://bitso.com/ with toml_file null). Probed 2026-10-22: toml_fetch
returns HTTP 404 (https://bitso.com/.well-known/stellar.toml), so no SEP-31
receive capability was verified and no corridor manifest was written.
Each entry in `anchors` records curator-declared context (name, ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 countries, kind, directory/manifest source, and date added). Countries
and `kind` are curator-declared metadata, NOT attested facts; `domains` mirrors
`anchors[].domain` in order.
